exposure: planned mode of delivery (planned vaginal birth vs. repeat cesarean after a previous cesarean delivery)
oxytocin induction or augmentation of labor
cohort: The study included all singleton births delivered at >=37 weeks' gestation in Nova Scotia, Canada, between 2003 and 2021, with one previous cesarean and no trial of labor contraindications.
finding: Planned vaginal birth, compared to a repeat cesarean after a previous cesarean delivery, was increasingly associated with severe maternal and perinatal-neonatal morbidity over time, with increased oxytocin induction and augmentation identified as a potential contributing factor.
mod_finding: The association between planned vaginal birth and severe maternal and perinatal-neonatal morbidity strengthened over time compared to repeat cesarean, with a notable increase in oxytocin induction/augmentation potentially contributing to worsening outcomes.
